title: SLPP opposes move to extend judges’ retirement age - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) has strongly criticised the government's reported move to extend the retirement age of higher court judges, alleging that the proposal is politically motivated and poses a threat to democracy.

In a statement, SLPP General Secretary and Attorney-at-Law Sagara Kariyawasam described the proposal as a "despicable and shameless" attempt aimed at serving political interests, claiming that there is significant public opposition to the move.

He said the SLPP has consistently opposed the proposal, arguing that it would deal a serious blow to the country's democratic institutions.

Kariyawasam also welcomed the reported resolution passed by the Judges' Association opposing the proposal, stating that the judges themselves raising concerns over the move should be given serious consideration in a democratic society.

He further said the SLPP had previously called on Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa to unite all opposition parties in Parliament to oppose the proposed extension of the retirement age of higher court judges.

The SLPP General Secretary reaffirmed the party's commitment to safeguarding democracy, stating that it would continue to oppose the proposal regardless of any threats or pressure.

title: Irrigation Department urges water conservation amid El Niño concerns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - The Irrigation Department has urged the public, including farmers, to use water sparingly in view of a possible El Niño situation in the future.

Director of Water Management H. M. P. S. D. Herath said that 80 reservoirs currently hold around 48% of their total capacity, adding that the available water is expected to be sufficient.

He highlighted the importance of conserving water resources to ensure availability during potential dry conditions.

title: Project launched to upgrade three Mullaitivu sports grounds - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - A project to develop three sports grounds in the Mullaitivu District to national standards was launched today with the laying of foundation stones under the patronage of Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Sunil Kumara Gamage and Vanni District MP Dr. Sellaththamby Thilakanathan.

The project aims to upgrade the selected grounds with running tracks, athletics facilities and other modern infrastructure to improve sports opportunities for young athletes in the district.

Addressing the event, Minister Gamage said the government is committed to ensuring equal opportunities for youth across the country, adding that sports infrastructure should be developed in all districts, regardless of geography.

He said the initiative is part of a nationwide programme to decentralise sports development and provide athletes from every region with access to quality training facilities.

Vanni District MP Dr. Thilakanathan described the project as the largest sports infrastructure development initiative implemented for Mullaitivu's youth in decades, noting that it would help promote healthy lifestyles, discipline and national unity.

Senior officials of the Ministry of Sports, local political representatives, district sports officers, schoolchildren and athletes attended the inauguration ceremony.

title: Rise in online indirect fraud reported: SLCERT - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (SLCERT) has reported an increase in indirect fraud incidents occurring in cyberspace.

Chief Information Security Engineer of SLCERT Charuka Damunupola said that more than 100 complaints related to such incidents have been received over the past month.

He urged the public to remain vigilant when engaging in online activities and to be cautious of suspicious messages, links and requests for personal information.

title: Police recover cache of weapons used in deadly Negombo Prison riot - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - Police have recovered a cache of sharp weapons and makeshift clubs during ongoing investigations into the recent riot at the Negombo Prison, where inmates brutally attacked prison officers.

According to the police, the sweep of the prison complex led to the discovery of hundreds of clubs, numerous sharp weapons, and a large stash of iron rods hidden inside the premises.

Investigations by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) revealed that during the height of the unrest, inmates broke into the prison kitchen to arm themselves. In addition to seizing sharp culinary tools, the rioters reportedly carried out coconuts from the kitchen to pelt and assault the prison officers.

The violent tragedy at the Negombo Prison claimed the lives of eight prison officials and 21 inmates. Following the incident, the CID launched a  probe into the clashes, leading to the latest recovery of weapons used during the fatal unrest.

title: SJB member arrested for illegal gun possession - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - An Ambalangoda Pradeshiya Sabha member representing the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has been arrested by the Galle District Crime Division for allegedly possessing a repeater gun illegally.

Police have launched investigations into how the councillor obtained the firearm and whether it had been used in any criminal activities.

title: Star Sports to air Lanka Premier League Season 6 from July 17 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Indian Television - The boundary ropes are going up, and so are expectations. The sixth edition of the Lanka Premier League (LPL) is ready to bowl into action, with Star Sports set to bring the tournament to Indian viewers as Sri Lanka’s flagship T20 competition returns from July 17 to August 8.

Organised by Sri Lanka Cricket and commercially managed by Innovative Production Group FZ (IPG), this year’s tournament will feature 94 cricketers, comprising 62 Sri Lankan players and 32 overseas stars, underlining the league’s growing international footprint.

The rising stature of the competition is reflected in the response from overseas players. According to the organisers, the sixth season attracted more than 650 registrations from players across 21 countries, making it one of the league’s strongest international turnouts to date.

The player roster blends established global names with local talent. International stars such as Moeen Ali, Jimmy Neesham, Shakib Al Hasan, Taskin Ahmed, Wanindu Hasaranga, Angelo Mathews, Kusal Mendis and Dasun Shanaka are set to feature, while Indian all-rounder Vijay Shankar will make his LPL debut.

The tournament continues to position itself as a platform where emerging Sri Lankan cricketers can compete alongside some of the world’s leading T20 players, gaining exposure in a high-profile franchise environment.

Commenting on the upcoming season, IPG Group founder and CEO Anil Mohan Sankhdhar and the league’s official rights holder, said the record international interest reflects the LPL’s growing standing within the global cricket calendar. He added that the league aims not only to stage a successful tournament but also to strengthen Sri Lankan cricket by creating opportunities for emerging talent while delivering a world-class experience for fans.

Lanka Premier League tournament director Samantha Dodanwela said Season 6 represents another important step in the league’s evolution, highlighting the blend of international stars and homegrown players expected to deliver another competitive edition of T20 cricket.

With a packed schedule, a strong overseas contingent and Indian audiences able to tune in on Star Sports, the Lanka Premier League is once again looking to turn Sri Lanka’s cricketing passion into a month-long spectacle that extends well beyond its shores.

title: Minor court judges oppose proposed Constitutional amendment on judges’ retirement age - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - The Judicial Service Association of Sri Lanka (JSASL), the sole organisation representing all District Court Judges and Magistrates in the country, has unanimously passed a resolution opposing the proposed Constitutional amendment aimed at extending the retirement age of judges of the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal, sources told the Daily Mirror.

According to sources, the resolution was adopted at a special general meeting convened by the JSASL this morning. All 65 members who attended the meeting voted unanimously in favour of the resolution rejecting the proposed amendment.

The proposed Constitutional amendment seeks to increase the retirement age of judges serving in the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal.

Meanwhile, sources further revealed that JSASL President Magistrate Pasan Amarasena had tendered his resignation from the presidency prior to the commencement of the special general meeting.

title: South Africa World Cup midfielder Adams dies aged 25
summary: South Africa and Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder Jayden Adams has died at the age of 25, just weeks after featuring for his country at the World Cup.

title: Sri Lanka’s disaster preparedness inadequate due to climate threats: DMC Chief - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) - Disaster Management Centre (DMC) Director General Retired Major General Sampath Kotuwegoda has warned that Sri Lanka faces an increased risk of disasters due to climate change and global warming.

Speaking before the Committee on Public Enterprises (COPE), he said the DMC lacks sufficient staff and resources to respond effectively to major disasters, noting that the institution faced severe challenges during Cyclone Ditwah.

He said the DMC’s Emergency Operations Centre, which operates 24 hours a day, lacks proper facilities for officers on night duty, while district disaster management units face delays in responding to emergencies occurring after office hours.

The Director General said although steps have been taken to merge the DMC with the National Disaster Relief Service Centre to address staff shortages, the process would take time and could create difficulties if another major disaster occurs.

He also warned that Sri Lanka remains vulnerable to a tsunami, stating that waves from a tsunami saying that near the Andaman Islands could reach the country within about 40 minutes, making the evacuation of millions of coastal residents a major challenge. He added that existing tsunami warning towers are currently not functioning and need repairs.

title: Special train services to be introduced for Nallur Festival – Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 11 (Daily Mirror) -Following criticism over the recent reduction of train services to the Northern Province ahead of the annual Nallur Kandaswamy Temple festival, Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake said that the Government is planning to introduce special train services to facilitate devotees travelling to major religious festivals.

Speaking in Parliament during the oral questions session, the Minister said recommendations have already been made to operate special train services during the festival season to ensure that devotees can travel conveniently.

He said sacred religious sites such as the Nallur Kandaswamy Temple, the Madhu Shrine, and the Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth) in Kandy are important places of worship that are visited by people of all faiths.

“Nallur, Madhu and the Sri Dalada Maligawa in Kandy are sacred religious destinations. They are not places visited only by followers of a particular religion but are important places of worship that people of all faiths visit and pay their respects,” the Minister said.

Rathnayake said that the Northern railway line has now been fully restored, allowing trains to operate at speeds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour.

“The Northern railway line has now been completely rehabilitated. Accordingly, trains are currently capable of operating at speeds of between 100 and 110 kilometres per hour,” he said.

While acknowledging that there are still some minor shortcomings in the railway service, the Minister assured Parliament that the Government would take every necessary step to provide uninterrupted, safe and convenient transport services during the upcoming festival season.

“Although there are a few minor shortcomings, all necessary measures will be taken to ensure uninterrupted, safe and convenient transport services for the public during the forthcoming festival season,” he said.
